intervals.quote: Kamioka Observatory is located in Gifu prefecture, Japan. The observatory was established in 1995

name: Kamioka Observatory (ICRR, University of Tokyo)
notes: The observatory also hosts KAGRA, CANDLES, NEWAGE and XENONnT R&D according to the ICRR facility page; only the Super-Kamiokande and Hyper-Kamiokande sites are recorded here.

The 1995 founding date is when ICRR's own page says the 'Kamioka Observatory' as a named administrative facility was established; it is not the date underground physics began at this site. The Mozumi mine location was already in scientific use well before 1995 — Kamiokande (experiment:kamiokande) started taking data there in 1983, and Super-Kamiokande's cavity excavation (experiment:super-kamiokande, detector:super-kamiokande) began in December 1991, both years before the observatory's formal 1995 establishment. This produces an expected 'experiment starts before its host facility' validator warning on both records; it is not an error in the sourced dates, just a mismatch between the mine's long history of use and the administrative facility's later formal founding.

summary.plain: An underground laboratory inside a mine in the Japanese Alps, a kilometre beneath a mountain. The rock above screens out most cosmic rays, so very rare signals from neutrinos can be seen.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory of the Institute for Cosmic Ray Research, University of Tokyo, in the Kamioka mine at Hida, Gifu. About 1000 m of rock (2700 m.w.e.) above Super-Kamiokande in the Mozumi mine; the Hyper-Kamiokande cavern is being built about 8 km south in the Tochibora mine.
